page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a decorative ornament band between two verse passages; a heading below the ornament; a woodcut initial at the start of the Latin verse; a catchword-like word at right at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: NEREI VATICINIVM DE Ruina classis Ibericae.
main_text.p: OVVM Gentis tumidus rector Iberica Audaci peteret classe Britannicum Littus: quum celebres turpia tenderet Anglos sub iuga mittere:
Ingratum cupidis navibus ocium Turbato posuit Nereus aequore, Praevisas cecinit dum properantibus Clades, fataque proxima.
Lugubri patrias deseris alite Oras, Classis, ait. Quo ruis impetu Praeceps? O, quid agis? fortiter occupa Portum. Nunc quid Ibericis Regnis

page.notes: The first verse lines are italic. The heading NEREI VATICINIVM DE Ruina classis Ibericae is set in spaced capitals. The initial O is a large woodcut letter, joined to VVM as printed. "Regnis" at the right foot is the catchword. Some words are doubtful in the scan, notably "Praeceps? O" and "agis?fortiter", which are printed with question marks as shown.
